title: kith-peer: outbox worker loop
description:
What: Implement the outbox worker loop as an async tokio task that polls OutboxStore.get_due() and attempts Peer/deliver to each due recipient.

Algorithm:
1. Define async fn outbox_worker(store: Arc<Mutex<Store>>, client: PeerHttpClient) -> ! (never returns)
2. Loop:
   a. Sleep 30 seconds via tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(30))
   b. Get now_unix = SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_secs() as i64
   c. Acquire store lock; call store.outbox().get_due(now_unix) -> on Err: log "outbox get_due failed: {err}", continue loop
   d. Release store lock before HTTP calls
   e. For each OutboxEntry in due list (process serially in Phase 1):
      i. Acquire store lock; look up contact by entry.peer_user_id via store.contacts().get_by_peer_user_id; release lock
      ii. If contact not found or contact.blocked: call outbox.record_failure(&entry.message_id, "contact not found or blocked", now_unix); continue
      iii. Build peer JMAP URL: format!("https://{}/jmap/api", contact.mailbox_host)
      iv. Acquire store lock; call store.messages().get(&entry.message_id) to load message payload; release lock
      v. Call client.deliver(&url, &message_payload).await
      vi. On Ok: acquire lock; call store.outbox().mark_delivered(&entry.message_id) and store.messages().update_delivery_state(&id, &DeliveryState::Delivered, Some(now_unix)); release lock; log "delivered {id}"
      vii. On Err: acquire lock; call store.outbox().record_failure(&entry.message_id, &err.to_string(), now_unix); release lock; log "delivery failed {id}: {category}"
3. Never unwrap() on lock acquisition; the Mutex is fair and should not poison in normal operation

Defensive rules:
- NEVER hold store lock across an .await (deadlock risk)
- Log error category, NOT message content or full URL
- Must not panic on network error; log and continue to next entry
- Contact must be re-validated before each delivery attempt (contact may have been blocked since enqueue)
- Phase 1: process due entries serially (one at a time); concurrent delivery is Phase 2

Agent team: Researcher R reads OutboxStore, MessageStore, ContactStore signatures. Implementer I writes outbox_worker function. Tester T writes tests verifying retry scheduling and success path using an in-memory SQLite store + mock PeerHttpClient. Validator V runs cargo test + clippy.

Tests (oracle = kith-architecture.md outbox retry spec):
- Due entry with valid contact -> deliver called, mark_delivered called, outbox row deleted
- Due entry with blocked contact -> record_failure called, deliver NOT called, outbox row stays with incremented attempt_count
- Network error -> record_failure called with error string; subsequent get_due respects next_attempt_at backoff
- 10th failure -> record_failure internally calls mark_failed; message.delivery_state = Failed
